text: Understanding Git branching is essential for modern software development. A branch lets you work on new features without affecting the main code. Developers create feature branches to build and test changes safely. Once the work is complete, they merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams often open pull requests so others can review the code and suggest improvements. This version control workflow keeps projects organised and reduces mistakes. It also allows several developers to work at the same time without conflicts. By using branches, merging, and pull requests together, teams can collaborate smoothly and keep their code stable.
